findings.text: named_lane_request_waiting passes project=project to runs.list_live, so the waiting population is scoped to the dispatching project, while its own docstring at placement.py:120 states the population is host-wide because one reservation seats every project's workers. A codex request queued in project B therefore does not hold the reserve for a local dispatch in project A, and project A fills the shared roster the request is waiting behind — the starvation the reserve exists to prevent, in the multi-project case. Dropping the project= argument is the whole repair.

The queued reason is hardcoded as "the placement reservation's roster is full (occupancy/limit)" at preparation.py:1149 and again at :1343, but _refuse_over_concurrency_ceiling raises RosterFull from whichever of the roster, partition-cores or memory bound actually binds (dispatch_admission.py:301-322), so a dispatch held at the cores or memory bound is reported to the coordinator as a full roster, with occupancy taken from this backend's live runs and limit from the binding bound. The accurate bound_refusal_text survives only in the unprinted 'detail' key, which makes the coordinator-facing reason wrong precisely for the cores-bound case the plan's done_when names.
